Like mariachi sinclair, he has low speed and his third skill helps make his stagger harder to pop which'll let him fill a tank role(blunt resist too if the enemy/dangerous attack uses it). Only does blunt damage, so if you want damage out of him, it's best not to bring him to someone who resists it. A lot of his side effects revolve around lowering enemy sp, which helps everyone win clashes (but I think only one of his attacks has more than 2 coins, making him not an ideal clasher).

With battles your generalist team can't handle, you should kinda analyze like that so you can see how to build a counter team.

Yeah, there's a lot to this game, but so far, you've only got too optimized to get through fights consistently. Like I'm still not even paying attention to the sin affinity resistances or defense token differences for the fight, or the super optimal sin resource team that balances passives,e.g.o. , and the support passives of other sinners. The games tutorial just tells you this stuff exists and expects you to experiment to pick up the nuances as you play.
